Register of Papers which on this day by the Honorable Commander Adriaan van Ommer and Council of Malabar at Cochin, via Ceylon with the ships departing from there were sent to the Fatherland to the Noble, Esteemed, Honorable Gentlemen Directors of the General Dutch chartered East India Company, at the Illustrious Assembly of Seventeen, within Amsterdam No. 1. An original letter by and to as above mentioned, dated this day by the Honorable Political Council to as aforesaid, under date 10th March in the year [1694], with all its attachments one after another in small format, and per the ship Courtgena sent toward Persia, in order to obtain further address from there via the customary land route; but because the aforementioned vessel was unable to gain the journey in that direction, it was brought back here again: 2. No. [2] Copy of letter dated 25th August of this year by the Political Council at Cochin to their Honorable Esteemed Excellencies at Batavia sent by post 6. No. 4. Copy of exchanged letters between the Company's merchant Baba Porboe, and Commander Adriaan van Ommen, and Council of Malabar — four documents with the Company's Sammorin, and likewise 2 similar documents exchanged by Commander with various letters and extracts, as translated documents, exchanged between the servants at Ceylon, the Tenggapatnam resident, the Company's Celormna, prince of Signatij, their rajahs, and merchants, and the Commander together with the Council of Malabar, concerning the plundering of the Company's lodge at Gapann: as well as Copy translated letters in the form of petition letters by Commander van Ommen to the Queen of Attingé, regarding and concerning the aforementioned plundering of the lodge and the shameful robbery of the Company's goods that had been there, and by her Majesty's response thereto given five documents exchanged translated documents with the aforementioned Commander, and the rajah of Calicut. Copy Instruction to the under-merchant Matthijs Dircks:

at Gapann: as well as Copy translated letters in the form of petition letters by Commander van Ommen to the Queen of Attingé, regarding and concerning the aforementioned plundering of the lodge and the shameful robbery of the Company's goods that had been there, and by her Majesty's response thereto given five documents exchanged translated documents with the aforementioned Commander, and the rajah of Calicut. Copy Instruction to the under-merchant Matthijs Dircks: Sonsbeek, and an assistant Jacob Valoth, in Commission to the northern Comptoirs for regulation also given, accompanied by the report by the aforementioned persons upon their return home from the north on 5th May last delivered in Council here No 11. 12. 13. No. 10: Copy report made by the under-merchant and rajah Lonistaispil, to the Political Council at Cochin dated 6th May last, regarding his execution concerning the King Sammorin at the court at Shavel Cattoe. Copy report by the appointed Gentlemen the Captain Lieutenant Cornelis Blikland, the warehouse master Leendert Blanckert, and the under-merchant Louis Taijispil, regarding their — execution concerning the rajah of Calicut and Porca, delivered orally in Political Council here. Report made by the assistant formerly resident of Wingurla Jacob Trogh, concerning the overrunning of that lodge by the Mogul field commander Serbatcham, and the capture and carrying off of the aforementioned resident to the lands of Pouda, and other adversities more brought upon the aforementioned Trogh by that gentleman. --- CHUNK 5 ---
Satria. To the Noble, High, Esteemed Gentlemen The Gentlemen Directors At the Assembly of Seventeen. Representing the General Dutch chartered East India Company Amsterdam. Noble, High, Esteemed, Commanding Gentlemen. — It was on the 30th of December of the recently passed year 1693, when we last had the honor of writing to your Noble High Esteemed Excellencies, and to make briefly known the condition of this coast according to the circumstances of the time, addressed to the Noble Gentleman Extraordinary Councillor of India and Governor, Thomas van Rhee, and Council at Ceylon, in order that with the return ships the Voorboog and Faam your Noble High Esteemed Excellencies would be brought to, and since we have no reason to doubt the safe passage of those vessels (which we hope God the Lord will have granted:) we shall request your Noble High Esteemed Excellencies to graciously accept the copy of that letter enclosed herein, pass by, and respectfully say in this: that we according to our made promise, and highest obligation, have not failed to prepare our further reports, and on the 10th of March of this year per the ship Courtgena with such attachments as pertained thereto, and together copied or prepared, in order to be carried over the land route of Persia in the customary manner to your Noble High Esteemed Excellencies, but since we have had the misfortune that that vessel after three and a half months of struggling, on account of many encountered contrary winds and exceptionally strong currents running to the east, and mistaken course in place of the northern Hook Costa dos Picos, 70 miles lower and near the eastern hook Pica dos Hiljos having fallen, was unable to obtain, for the preservation of ship, men, and goods, it could not be recovered, through weakness of crew since by an extraordinary mortality at the inner water

--- CHUNK 1 ---
after three and a half months of sailing, on account of many encountered contrary winds and exceptionally strong currents running to the east, as well as a miscalculated course in place of the northern Cape Costa dos Picos, seventy miles lower, and having fallen near the eastern cape Pica dos Hiljos, we were unable to obtain, for the preservation of ship, men, and goods, what we could not retrieve further, due to weakness of personnel, since through an extraordinary mortality at the inner water we have already lost twenty-four dead, cast overboard, and besides those who lay sick in bed there, and eight Moors, we had only fourteen healthy men remaining who were capable of manning the helm, we turned back to this roadstead and fortunately, given the bad season, as it was on the twenty-eighth of June of this year in the mud bay that we were salvaged, and consequently the aforementioned our last letter was brought back, so it goes forth as now such an original: signed over, to whose contents we in all submission in this matter shall conduct ourselves, and further proceed to give knowledge to Your Excellency's high regard of what has occurred since in the service of the general Company under this Malabar command entrusted to us, and what has been accomplished, making a beginning with Wingurla, where your Excellency's high regard by the aforementioned our last reports shall have become clear that the Company's lodge was plundered by surprise by the Mughal field commander named Serbetgham, and the resident Jacob Trogh was taken captive to the fortress Ponda, likewise what efforts and exertions we have undertaken in the work, as well concerning the Mogul, as with him and the Dessai, or lord of the Wingurla lands named Kempsant for the return of that dwelling at cost and without loss to the Company, but as it appears to us, and for the first time nothing else is to be suspected, so shall such not easily follow, since the aforementioned field commander has taken the residence place

--- CHUNK 2 ---
Jacob Trogh was taken captive to the fortress Ponda, likewise what efforts and exertions we have undertaken in the work, as well concerning the Mogul, as with him and the Dessai, or lord of the Wingurla lands named Kempsant for the return of that dwelling at cost and without loss to the Company, but as it appears to us, and for the first time nothing else is to be suspected, so shall such not easily follow, since the aforementioned field commander has taken the residence place as a stronghold of the lower lands firmly in possession, and strengthened it with his military forces, having however released our resident after fourteen and a half months of captivity, and set him at liberty, only under the promise that when he himself in person with his army from above from Visiapour should appear there after the ending of the aforementioned bad season, and should have destroyed the rebellious Dessai, then the lodge at Wingurla no longer being needed would be returned to the Company, just as your Excellency's high regard may please to understand one and the other circumstance, by the writing of that Moorish commander in answer to our letter directed, as the copy report of aforesaid resident Jacob Trogh with his arrival here on the first of the current month was delivered to us, to whose contents we shall conduct ourselves in all respect, to be brief; the damage or the loss which the Company has suffered by the overrunning of that lodge is indeed not of such importance, amounting only to approximately seventy chans or 4,793 guilders, 8 stivers, 2 deniers [modern equivalent: Dutch guilders], as well as the affront brought upon her Excellency thereby, but since through the continual upheavals and disturbances of those lands through war it is not to be apprehended that the Company's trade in some years there will yet be restored as it formerly was under peaceful governance, and it is to be trusted

--- CHUNK 3 ---

The dispatch and sending of the small vessels the Jager and Plasluijs to the lands of Coudewaar or Uurzee on the seventeenth of February of this year, loaded with various merchandise in order according to the resolution drawn up in council of Malabar, under the guidance and care of the under-merchant and Cashier Matthijs Dircksz. Sonsbeek and first assistant Jacob Valosh—for the benefit of the Company to be put to use, your Excellency's high regard was made known by the aforementioned our most humble last communication; and since it is our duty to inform your Excellency's high regard in this matter further to report what success that dispatch has had, so we say that the aforementioned appointed commissioners on the first of May—having returned there, have given us such a report or account of their accomplishment, as under No. 9 in copy herewith goes, whereby your Excellency's high regard shall then come to see that through their

--- CHUNK 4 ---
aforementioned our most humble last communication; and since it is our duty to inform your Excellency's high regard in this matter further to report what success that dispatch has had, so we say that the aforementioned appointed commissioners on the first of May—having returned there, have given us such a report or account of their accomplishment, as under No. 9 in copy herewith goes, whereby your Excellency's high regard shall then come to see that through their negotiation of the following merchandise, namely: 33,705 pounds Japanese copper rod at 16 per 125 pounds per 4,314 guilders, 12 stivers, 5 deniers. 20,972 pounds tin at 16 per 500 pounds per 671 guilders, 2 stivers, 6 deniers. 2,699½ pounds thin at 45½ per pound per 166 guilders. Quicksilver at 29⅓ per pound per 9,623 guilders, 3 stivers, 7 deniers. Vermillion at 300 per pound per 75 guilders, 280 stivers. Foelij or mace at 480 per pound per 268 guilders, 2 stivers, 5 deniers. 250 pounds cloves at 4 guilders, 65 stivers per pound per 232½ guilders. Sum per pound 5,904 guilders, 129/900 stivers, outside all expenses, purely for the Company's profit a sum of 15,293 guilders, 7 stivers, 6 deniers, or per pound 27,189/900 stivers, which in case it had been undertaken somewhat earlier in time through the sale of the remaining goods would apparently have fallen out more abundantly, therefore such has been taken into consideration by us, and having been weighed the further instances

--- CHUNK 5 ---

Sum per pound 5,904 guilders, 129/900 stivers, outside all expenses, purely for the Company's profit a sum of 15,293 guilders, 7 stivers, 6 deniers, or per pound 27,189/900 stivers, which in case it had been undertaken somewhat earlier in time through the sale of the remaining goods would apparently have fallen out more abundantly, therefore such has been taken into consideration by us, and having been weighed the further instances and demands of the Company's broker at Wingurla Mortoneijck and a certain Brahmin merchant named Antaweijck at Ancola, under the jurisdiction of Uurzee dwelling, in order to be able to obtain again some trading goods, so it is that we by resolution in our council for the greatest service of the general Company's good have found it fitting and have resolved, the small vessel the Tambour being on the eighteenth of November last arrived with a parcel of negotiated slaves for Ceylon from Cape of Good Hope No. 19 via Madagascar to provision itself with water and firewood at this roadstead; we have these serviceable people unloaded here on land and sent the ship Silverstein in place of the aforementioned small vessel, which otherwise, inasmuch as the Noble Lord Governor Thomas van Rhee and Council by their missive dated the eighth and ninth of November past expressed their inability, to have ship's opportunity from there to sail hither, for the fatherland's return to Ceylon having ordered to be used for that purpose, and to be unloaded with the aforementioned merchandise, namely: 125,000 pounds Japanese copper rod 1,000 cloves 1,000 foelij 1,000 nutmeg 300 cinnamon 10,000 tin 250 vermillion 250 benzoin 5 green cloth 150 pounds camphor 5 pieces red scarlet cloth. Since the Company through the exchange of that merchandise, pro rata the cost and selling price according to the Surat market or price current in conformity with the esteemed order of her high Excellency's regard at Batavia henceforth at this

--- CHUNK 1 ---
the aforementioned merchant goods, namely: 125,000 pounds of Japanese rod copper, 1,000 nails, 1,000 foully [uncertain: original term], 300 nutmeg, 10,000 cinnamon, 250 tin, 250 vermillion, 5 benzouin [benzoin], 150 pounds green cloth, 5 camphor, sticks of red scarlet cloth. Since the Honourable Company, in the exchange of these merchant goods, pro rata according to the cost and selling price according to the Surat market or price current, in conformity with the esteemed order of their High Noble and Honourable Excellencies at Batavia, henceforth to be maintained on this coast in the selling of the Company's merchandise, has been calculated and reckoned, there stands to be gained a clear profit of ƒ70,115.19.-, and for the furtherance of which, according to what is required, we have appointed and committed experienced and capable ministers, namely the under-merchant Johannes Wighmans and the assistants David van Orlei and Jacob Trogh. For, under submission to wiser judgment, if it should continue in such manner yearly, we consider it sufficiently beneficial for the service of the Honourable Company, as has been observed, as one must continually be subject to the violence which one has had to suffer so many years in succession from the government on this coast of Janara, and which cannot be avoided by any reasonable means, particularly when the Honourable Company, requiring rice for its consumption, has always had to pay for it more dearly, or has been forced to accept it, whereas all private merchants have the freedom to buy that grain at the bazaar or market price for less, as it appears to be a point in which the Queen or the government finds itself interested, and which, not lightly, according to merchant custom, will allow other foreign court-minded persons that privilege. To which I believe alone a sufficient proof may serve the recently concluded Contract by the late Honourable Commander Isaac van Dielen, of blessed memory, in his personal presence there on that coast, between that princess and the Company. For not only has it failed,

--- CHUNK 2 ---
to buy, as it appears to be a point in which the Queen or the government finds itself interested, and which, not lightly, according to merchant custom, will allow other foreign court-minded persons that privilege. To which I believe alone a sufficient proof may serve the recently concluded Contract by the late Honourable Commander Isaac van Dielen, of blessed memory, in his personal presence there on that coast, between that princess and the Company. For not only has it failed, as your Excellency has already been informed, in the obtaining of the contracted merchant goods, but also according to the writing of the resident stationed there, Hendrik Wijnhout, when one believed, as the content of the aforementioned Contract shows, that free and unencumbered trade had been obtained, to be able to conduct business with any merchant without interference from the government, it has been experienced and discovered how miserably one has been deceived in this regard, and all labour, trouble, and costs expended thereon have turned out to be in vain and fruitless. For, as we have mentioned before, the commissioners Sonsbeek and Valoth in their journey to Mir Sea, in the Instruction given to them as their regulation, were so earnestly recommended to procure 150 loads of rice for the urgent need of this city and its subordinate Comptoir, that it has been impossible for the resident Wijnhout to obtain the same, increased to 200 loads, for less than, in conformity with the prices of the preceding years of 17 pagodas per load, apart from the freight charges of 3 1/3 pagodas per load, which have had to be paid to an inland bark for the transport here. Thus the cost per load for the Company comes to stand at approximately 22 pagodas, which is certainly quite dear. But against this, with matters lying so, nothing else can be said than to wish for the service of the general Company that the trade in that kingdom might be otherwise arranged. However, since it is not,

Thus the cost per load for the Company comes to stand at approximately 22 pagodas, which is certainly quite dear. But against this, with matters lying so, nothing else can be said than to wish for the service of the general Company that the trade in that kingdom might be otherwise arranged. However, since it is not, and what your High Noble and Honourable Excellencies, the High Indian government at Batavia, having well understood this, have been pleased by your High Noble and Honourable Excellencies' esteemed missive dated the 20th of August last to command us that the Comptoir, as being of no further use to the Honourable Company, should be closed, or at least until such time as some other expedient can be devised to bring about some improvement in that regard and to establish the interest of the Honourable Company with greater advantage in that place. Thus we are also resolved to let this take effect forthwith. However, notwithstanding this, to the conviction of the Honourable Company's upright dealings, and as one is accustomed to hold and fulfil one's given word and promise, particularly in all written agreements entered into, so as never to be able to be blamed or spoken ill of on that account, the two elephants promised by the latest Contract by the Queen and the realm's administrator, which were summoned from Ceylon in the past year and brought here by the ship the Unicorn in the month of March of this year, we intend to send with the first opportunity, in conformity with your High Noble and Honourable Excellencies at Batavia's greatly esteemed command and good intention, and to present them to their Highnesses. Meanwhile, setting aside this unpleasant matter, we turn to Cannanore [Kannur], regarding which your Excellency can presently form no other judgment than that the fortification

--- CHUNK 4 ---
the past year from Ceylon summoned, and brought here by the ship the Unicorn in the month of March of this year, we intend to send with the first opportunity, in conformity with your High Noble and Honourable Excellencies at Batavia's greatly esteemed command and good intention, and to present them to their Highnesses. Meanwhile, setting aside this unpleasant matter, we turn to Cannanore [Kannur], regarding which your Excellency can presently form no other judgment than that the fortification works, warehouses, and dwelling houses being so greatly fallen into decay, we have resolved to summon the merchant and chief of that fortress, Adam van der Duijn, here, on the occasion that our subordinate yacht the Jager, laden with various merchant goods and necessities, was dispatched there on the 28th of the past month, and is to return. In order, according to the authority of your High Noble and Honourable Excellencies at Batavia, to have obtained from him not only information on that account, but also on the state and situation of the trade, as well as the prospects that might exist there for making some improvement, having taken the proper information, we may then be capable of giving your Excellency the nearest knowledge thereof, and by us it shall be deemed good to order this to be carried out to the greatest service of the Honourable Company. And likewise regarding the city of Cochin, since Commander Adriaan van Ommen has been appointed by your High Noble and Honourable Excellencies at Batavia as Commander in place of the deceased Honourable Isaac van Dielen, of blessed memory, to take over the chief administration on this coast, arriving here on the 11th of November of the last month that has passed with the fluyt ship Hobree, he has not yet had sufficient time, as is proper, and also his most important work to be done, in consideration of the true service of the general Company and in compliance with the orders and commands of the aforementioned your High Excellencies at Batavia's careful

--- CHUNK 5 ---
the deceased Honourable Isaac van Dielen, of blessed memory, to take over the chief administration on this coast, arriving here on the 11th of November of the last month that has passed with the fluyt ship Hobree, he has not yet had sufficient time, as is proper, and also his most important work to be done, in consideration of the true service of the general Company and in compliance with the orders and commands of the aforementioned your High Excellencies at Batavia's careful inspection, both regarding the repair of the fallen fortification works as well as the trade and other matters to be undertaken. Thus we hope that your Excellency will be pleased to graciously allow him to defer and reserve this until the nearest time to fulfil his highest obligation, and to give a true report thereof in the coming months of February or March by the usual land route of Persia, as also to the aforementioned your High Excellencies at Batavia with the first opportunity occurring for that purpose. Meanwhile, since we cannot break off so soon from our duty to mention something of this and that matter, first of all regarding our meeting and negotiation with the King of Cochin. After the Commander, as said before, had arrived here, and according to the customary manner had made his arrival known to most of the surrounding Malabar kings and princes through dispatched envoys, the King of Cochin had his Excellency request to come meet him at his ordinary court here outside the city, while the mourning ceremonies for the recently deceased Queen were not yet concluded according to their law, he was unable to appear within the city himself. To which, however, an hour was agreed upon, so on the 26th of the past month, after some days before

--- CHUNK 1 ---
had made known, so the King of Cochin [Kochi] requested His Excellency to come meet him at his ordinary court here outside the city, while the mourning ceremonies for the recently deceased Queen were not yet concluded according to their law, making it impossible for him to appear within the city himself. To this end, after an hour had been agreed upon, the Commander on the 26th of the past month, after having been greeted and welcomed some days before by his Express-sent ambassador, accompanied by the members of the political Council in person, was in his presence. After sitting briefly and some complimentary remarks having been exchanged, he delivered to him the letter from the highly esteemed Lord Governor-General, written in response to his Majesty's dispatched correspondence, together with the gift goods which were sent on behalf of the Honored Company for his Majesty, and some small items which we additionally supplied, consisting of the following: One gold chain with a jewel set with pearls and precious stones; One piece of 24 carats of gold moiré; one of 64 [carats] of Holland velvet aurora color; 220 pounds of assorted spices, cloves, mace, and nutmeg; 627 [pounds] of sandalwood; 2 fine flintlock muskets; 2 gilded carbines; 2 cases of rose water. After receiving and carrying away these items, and after the contents of the aforementioned letter had been explained to him by our ordinary court-appointed ambassador or ambassador, the junior merchant Louis Taijspil, translated from Portuguese into the Malabar language and made understood to him, he expressed great satisfaction and joy thereupon, with good assurances and promises that the favor and regard which the Honored Company had shown and demonstrated toward his person, he would always acknowledge by endeavoring to advance the interests of the realm according to the true purpose and welfare of their Excellencies and his sub

--- CHUNK 2 ---
or ambassador, the junior merchant Louis Taijspil, translated from Portuguese into the Malabar language and made understood to him, he expressed great satisfaction and joy thereupon, with good assurances and promises that the favor and regard which the Honored Company had shown and demonstrated toward his person, he would always acknowledge by endeavoring to advance the interests of the realm according to the true purpose and welfare of their Excellencies and his subjects to take to heart, being assured that the Honored Company would never abandon him, nor fail to protect him against all his enemies and the unwilling, in such a way that his Majesty, for some time now since the death of the late Lord Commander Isaac van Dielen [Isaac van Dielen], had to suffer the opposite to his sorrow and great heart's pain, from which he now hoped that with the arrival of a new Lord Commander, he would be set at ease and henceforth be freed. Whereby he principally made clear the injustice and violence which the Samorin [Zamorin] had committed against him by taking away the fortress of Scherlevta [Sherlevta], and delivering the same contrary to the last concluded contract between the highly esteemed Lord Commissioner Hendrik Adriaan van Reede tot Drakestein [Hendrik Adriaan van Reede tot Drakestein], Lord of Mijdrecht, etc., and the Samorin, back to the expelled and rebellious northern lord Ainecoettij Nambeddij [Ainecoettij Nambeddij], and thus restoring the same to his full possession without the knowledge or consent of his Majesty or the Honored Company, hoping that their Excellencies would maintain him in all justice against this and strive that he would not be deprived of his right, but that the dominion over the said fortress would come into his hands, with the promise relying upon this, also that nothing hostile should be done against the Samorin on account of this, unless otherwise the interests of his realm might require it, and thus his

--- CHUNK 3 ---
of his Majesty or the Honored Company, to be restored, hoping that their Excellencies would maintain him in all justice against this and strive that he would be deprived of his right, but that the dominion over the said fortress would come into his hands, with the promise relying upon this, also that nothing hostile should be done against the Samorin on account of this, unless otherwise the interests of his realm might require it, and thus his right by arms to be preserved, without prior knowledge and consent of the Honored Company to be undertaken, to which he was promised by us with forceful and effective words, and further reasons serving the purpose having animated him, he took his leave from the other for that time, leaving the handling of the matters of principal importance to be deferred to a better opportunity. Meanwhile, the King Samorin also sent his ambassador from Pananij [Pananij], where he is presently staying, hither, and on the 4th of this month, having appeared here within the city and before us, the conversation held together with him was also directed only to the delivery of his master's greetings and the expression of satisfaction over the arrival of the Commander, as well as to excuse himself that his Majesty could not come to Cranganoor [Cranganore] at his court there upon our request, so that, as we otherwise intended, the Commander might personally meet him and be handed over the letter and gift goods likewise intended by their High Excellencies at Batavia for his Majesty, consisting of 1 piece of gold chain and 1 jewel for said chain, set with emeralds, rubies, and diamonds, and 4 pairs of fine pearls. To this end, bringing in response from ours such an ola [ola: a palm-leaf document], as their translations, appended under No. 5 herein, your Excellencies will come to see, and to whose contents we conduct ourselves with respect,

--- CHUNK 4 ---
and gift goods likewise intended by their High Excellencies at Batavia for his Majesty, consisting of 1 piece of gold chain and 1 jewel for said chain, set with emeralds, rubies, and diamonds, and 4 pairs of fine pearls. To this end, bringing in response from ours such an ola [ola: a palm-leaf document], as their translations, appended under No. 5 herein, your Excellencies will come to see, and to whose contents we conduct ourselves with respect. The principal reason for this was that his Majesty, being occupied with the necessary preparations for celebrating the twelve-year festival called Mamanga [Mamanga], which was now soon at hand, could not possibly undertake the journey to Cranganoor, and therefore it necessarily had to be postponed until after the conclusion of that great festival, which could only be honored by his Majesty's presence alone and no other way, which therefore cannot take place before the month of February or March of the coming year, unless the Commander, as his Majesty comes to request, could undertake to travel in person to Pananij to greet his Majesty at his court there. However, this could not be brought about and agreed upon with the constitution of the times and affairs concerning southern Malabar, which press more urgently, so until that time, although we shall be forced to hold many matters which are to be negotiated with the Samorin for the interest and benefit of the general Company in abeyance; except, however, those of such a nature that cannot admit of delay, and must be taken in hand and executed forthwith, particularly the settlement of the long-delayed differences with the Queen of Attingal [Attingal], over breach of alliance with the invocation and admission of the English in her realm for the continuation of a free trade, as many other improprieties and acts of violence
